metadata.note: The Chicago, Burlington and Quincy's Big Horn Basin main line - Billings, Montana south through Frannie, Lovell, Greybull, Worland and Thermopolis, through Wind River Canyon to Casper, and east down the North Platte to Orin Junction, 398 miles. This is the line the Cody Branch met at Frannie (see cbq_cody_branch.geojson), and the northern half of the route of the Shoshone, CB&Q/C&S trains 29 and 30, Denver to Billings. It was built in stages from both ends over nine years - Frannie south to Kirby 1905-07, Kirby to Thermopolis 1909, Fromberg to Warren 1911, Thermopolis to Casper through the Wind River Canyon tunnels October 20 1913, Casper to Orin Junction 1914 - which is why it is drawn as five features rather than one: a single feature would assert service through Wind River Canyon from 1905. All five carry the CB&Q's colour, including the Fromberg-to-Billings stretch that ran over Northern Pacific track, because the CB&Q ran the trains. Passenger service on the whole line ended with the Shoshone's last run on September 1 1967.
sources: https://www.wyohistory.org/encyclopedia/burlington-route-wyomings-second-transcontinental-railroad (construction chronology: Frannie October 3 1905, Kirby September 3 1907, Thermopolis 1909, Casper October 20 1913, Orin Junction 1914, Guernsey-Wendover cutoff December 15 1915, and the Big Horn Railroad Company)

not_yet_sourced: No timetable was read for this line. Every headway_min is an estimate and avg_speed_kmh is a guess; the number of daily trains in each era, and what ran besides the Shoshone, are unknown here.

The individual dates the rails reached Greybull, Basin, Worland, Lovell, Cowley and Deaver are not sourced - only that construction began at Frannie October 3 1905 and reached Kirby September 3 1907. The Frannie - Kirby feature is therefore drawn from 1907, which understates service at the northern towns by up to two years.
The year the Shoshone was first named is not sourced; the 1913/1914 segment boundaries mark when the through route opened, not when the train was inaugurated.

The Colorado and Southern portion of the Shoshone's route - Orin Junction south through Wendover, Wheatland and Cheyenne to Denver, plus the CB&Q's Guernsey-Wendover cutoff of December 15 1915 - is not drawn. It is a candidate for its own layer under the C&S, whose colour would need checking against the existing Fort Worth & Denver / C&S features under Rule 4.
The CB&Q's 1901-1911 approach from Toluca, Montana over Pryor Gap to Frannie is still not drawn; the alignment was lifted in April 1911 and is not in OpenStreetMap.
Branches off this line that carried passengers - notably Greybull west up the Greybull River, and the Riverton line off at Shoshoni - are not drawn.

properties.speed_source: estimated: Big Horn Basin main line with a daily through train and locals; no timetable running time was checked. Unsourced.
properties.geometry_quality: REAL TRACE, no approximated legs, in two parts. Frannie to the north end of the BNSF Casper Subdivision at Laurel, Montana is cut from the same continuous Casper Subdivision trace described on the other features in this layer. The last 15.19 mi from Laurel into Billings is traced over the ex-Northern Pacific main (OSM name='BNSF MRL 1st Subdivision'), because that is what the CB&Q's own trains did - its rails ended short of Billings and the last stretch was trackage over the NP, exactly as on the Lincoln - Alliance - Billings layer's Huntley-to-Billings end. A 2.6 mi out-and-back excursion into the Laurel yard that the router picked up has been trimmed, leaving zero excursions. Total -71.51 mi against 72 mi documented (Frannie milepost 600, Billings 672); the Billings end stops at the same point the Lincoln - Alliance - Billings layer ends, so the two meet. Simplified to a 20 m Douglas-Peucker tolerance (0 -> 0 points). Straight-line repair 2026-08-29: 1 ruled segment totalling 12 mi replaced with OpenStreetMap-traced rail geometry (see geometry_repairs for the OSM lines each one followed).

segments.note: Opened April 9 1911, when 30 miles of new track between Fromberg and Warren were completed. This replaced the Burlington's original approach to the Big Horn Basin over the Pryor Mountains from Toluca, Montana, which was torn up the same month - blamed on the grade in Pryor Gap, slow running, and the awkwardness of connecting at Coburn rather than Billings. From Fromberg the CB&Q's trains ran over Northern Pacific track through Silesia and Laurel into Billings; the Burlington's own rails ended at Fromberg. In these two years the Basin line still dead-ended at Thermopolis, so this was the way in and out. Frequency estimated/unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: the April 9 1911 completion of the 30-mile Fromberg-Warren connection, the simultaneous abandonment of Toluca-Warren and the reasons given for it are from the Pryor Mountains homestead-era railroad page; the Fromberg-Billings running over Northern Pacific track and the Frannie 600 / Fromberg 634 / Billings 672 mileposts are from John Fowler's Montana passenger stations compilation (SL 175), line 56 Frannie-Billings. Headway and speed are unsourced estimates.

segments.note: From October 20 1913 - and fully from 1914, when the Orin Junction connection put it in touch with the Colorado and Southern - this was a through main line, not a Basin stub. Its through passenger train was the Shoshone, CB&Q/C&S trains 29 and 30, Denver to Billings, 667 miles via Cheyenne, Wheatland, Casper, Thermopolis, Worland, Greybull and Lovell; in 1946 it carried heavyweight sleepers, a diner and reclining chair cars. By 1967 the name had been dropped and the train was a single modernised heavyweight coach and storage mail cars. It made its last run September 1 1967, which is where these years end. Frequency estimated/unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: the October 20 1913 arrival at Casper and the 1914 Orin Junction connection with the Colorado and Southern are from WyoHistory's Burlington Route article; the Shoshone's numbers (29/30), 667-mile Denver-Billings route, 1946 consist and September 1 1967 discontinuation are from Wikipedia. Headway and speed are unsourced estimates.

properties.geometry_quality: REAL TRACE, no approximated legs. Cut from a single continuous trace of the whole ex-CB&Q Big Horn Basin main line, built by shortest-path routing over the OpenStreetMap ways tagged name='BNSF Casper Subdivision' (367 ways, Laurel MT to Orin Junction WY - BNSF kept the CB&Q route as one subdivision, so the modern name covers the historic line end to end). The whole trace runs 397.03 mi against 398 mi of documented mileage (99.7%), with every checkable station landing within about a mile of its timetable milepost: Fromberg 360.2 traced vs 360 documented, Frannie 325.6 vs 326, Lovell 308.8 vs 308, Greybull 270.5 vs 271, Basin 263.1 vs 263, Manderson 254.1 vs 254, Worland 235.5 vs 235, Lucerne 210.1 vs 210, Thermopolis 202.9 vs 203, Bonneville 171.4 vs 171, Lysite 150.5 vs 150, Arminto 126.9 vs 126, Casper 68.8 vs 68, Glenrock 44.7 vs 44, Douglas 15.5 vs 15 (all as miles from Orin Junction). Zero gaps and zero out-and-back artifacts - the trace was checked for excursions that leave and rejoin the same point and none were found. Simplified to a 20 m Douglas-Peucker tolerance (0 -> 0 points). This feature is -110.6 mi of it. ERA CAVEAT: this is the modern alignment; the corridor has not been relocated, but any minor line changes within it are drawn in their present form.

segments.note: The Big Horn Basin line proper. Construction began at Frannie on October 3 1905 under the Big Horn Railroad Company, a CB&Q paper corporation set up while James J. Hill's group was planning a Gulf-to-Pacific route, and moved south along the Big Horn River through Greybull, Basin and Worland to reach Kirby on September 3 1907, where work stopped until 1909. Drawn from 1907 rather than 1905 because that is the date the whole of this segment was open - Greybull, Basin and Worland had trains earlier, but no source consulted gives their individual dates, so drawing from 1905 would assert service at Kirby that did not exist. Frequency estimated/unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: the October 3 1905 start at Frannie, the Big Horn Railroad Company, the route south through Greybull, Basin and Worland, and the September 3 1907 arrival at Kirby are from WyoHistory's Burlington Route article; station mileposts are from John Fowler's Wyoming passenger stations compilation (SL 170), line 10. The individual opening dates for Greybull, Basin and Worland are NOT SOURCED. Headway and speed are unsourced estimates.

segments.note: The hard part, and the piece that turned the Big Horn Basin stub into a main line: south from Thermopolis through Wind River Canyon, where blasting tunnels through the granite of the west wall held construction up for several years, then across the divide into the North Platte watershed to reach Casper on October 20 1913 - completing a rail circumnavigation of the Big Horn Mountains. From October 20 1913 - and fully from 1914, when the Orin Junction connection put it in touch with the Colorado and Southern - this was a through main line, not a Basin stub. Its through passenger train was the Shoshone, CB&Q/C&S trains 29 and 30, Denver to Billings, 667 miles via Cheyenne, Wheatland, Casper, Thermopolis, Worland, Greybull and Lovell; in 1946 it carried heavyweight sleepers, a diner and reclining chair cars. By 1967 the name had been dropped and the train was a single modernised heavyweight coach and storage mail cars. It made its last run September 1 1967, which is where these years end. segments.note: The last link. In 1914 the CB&Q ran east down the North Platte from Casper through Glenrock and Douglas to meet the Colorado and Southern at Orin Junction, which on paper created the shortest rail route from the Gulf of Mexico to the Pacific - and was promptly undercut by the opening of the Panama Canal the same year. Wyoming construction ended December 15 1915 with the Guernsey-Wendover cutoff, a better link to the C&S. This is where the Denver end of the Shoshone's route leaves CB&Q rails; the C&S line on south through Wendover, Wheatland and Cheyenne to Denver is not drawn in this layer. From October 20 1913 - and fully from 1914, when the Orin Junction connection put it in touch with the Colorado and Southern - this was a through main line, not a Basin stub. Its through passenger train was the Shoshone, CB&Q/C&S trains 29 and 30, Denver to Billings, 667 miles via Cheyenne, Wheatland, Casper, Thermopolis, Worland, Greybull and Lovell; in 1946 it carried heavyweight sleepers, a diner and reclining chair cars.
